#### 1. Houge-Janssens syndrome 4  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.483)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2467813, Reactome:R-HSA-2500257, Reactome:R-HSA-5663220, Reactome:R-HSA-68877)

**Proposed mechanism:** BUB1B (HGNC:1399) —DISRUPTS→ mitotic spindle assembly (GO:0000227); mitotic spindle assembly (GO:0000227) —LEADS_TO→ chromosome segregation (GO:0007049); chromosome segregation (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ Aneuploidy (HP:0001436); BUB1B (HGNC:1399) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); BUB1B (HGNC:1399) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252). Loss-of-function mutations in BUB1B disrupt normal mitotic spindle assembly, leading to errors in chromosome segregation. This results in aneuploidy, a hallmark of mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1 and a contributing factor to the developmental phenotypes seen in Houge-Janssens syndrome 4, including developmental delay and microcephaly.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in BUB1B are not found in individuals with mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1 or Houge-Janssens syndrome 4, or if these variants do not demonstrate a haploinsufficient functional consequence, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Any pathogenic variant found at a high frequency (>1%) in gnomAD populations would challenge its role as a rare disease causal variant.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BUB1B in cell cycle regulation and chromosome segregation provides a potential therapeutic target for both conditions. Modulating pathways that correct spindle assembly or aneuploidy could offer a unified treatment approach.
